response.observation: The previous fix was applied in `get_order_by` at compile time, which broke `test_order_raises_on_non_selected_column` because it silently adds ANY missing column to the select rather than only preserving ordering fields that existed before the select was narrowed. Additionally, the code had a string-formatting bug (`RawSQL('%d' % (len(self.select), ()))` — the tuple makes `%` format fail). The correct fix is at the `Query.set_values` level: when the select is narrowed by `values()`/`values_list()`, preserve any concrete model-field names still referenced by existing `order_by` entries, appending them after the user-requested fields. This way the ordering column remains in the positional select for combinator queries, while `values_select` ensures the column propagates to inner union queries. Cases where ordering is added AFTER values narrowing (like the existing test) are unaffected because `set_values` is not called again.
